data.one_liner: Composable animations, spring effects, and scroll transitions using modifier syntax.
data.what_it_does: Allows developers to apply animations, transitions, and effects directly onto Flutter widgets using a SwiftUI-inspired modifier syntax. Supports state-driven triggers, spring physics, keyframe timelines, and scroll-linked viewport effects without needing explicit AnimationControllers.
use_when: You want to build widget animations or scroll transitions with minimal boilerplate.
You need spring physics and state-driven triggers without managing AnimationControllers.
You want SwiftUI-style modifier syntax directly inside the Flutter widget tree.
avoid_when: You are using complex vector graphics engines like Rive or Lottie.
You prefer imperative timeline management via standalone animation controllers.
strengths: Declarative modifier syntax integrates cleanly into the widget tree.
Built-in scroll transitions react smoothly to viewport position without manual scroll listeners.
Supports springs, keyframe timelines, and layout-driven size animations.
weaknesses: Not suited for heavy vector illustrations or animations exported from design software.
Documentation outside of the README and API reference is still growing.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a chainable extension-based animation library with a slightly different set of presets and built-in effects.

alternatives.name: animate_do
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you just need standard preset entrance animations packaged as ready-to-use widgets.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need to render complex vector animations designed in After Effects.

data.minimal_example:
Icon(Icons.favorite)
    .scale(selected ? 1.2 : 1)
    .animate(
      trigger: selected,
      motion: const CupertinoMotion.snappy(),
    )
